findings.observation: A single long multi-blade claw is visible on the raised screen-left hand. The extended opposite screen-right hand is a small dark glove and has no second long claw. The previously reported duplicated long weapon is not present in this final rendered pose.

Head, torso and armored boots remain within the same SD body range across the HQ/premium joins. The HQ slash folds the legs and brings the arm across the body; premium extends into a lunge. No large simultaneous head-and-body scale swap, extra visible arm, detached boot or clipping was identified. Hair, coat and weapon reach change the outer bounds and are not treated as body-scale errors.

Premium recovery is slightly broader through the boots and outer hair/coat silhouette than the support poses. The polish-to-idle body remains close in head/torso/boot scale; no conspicuous whole-body replacement was observed. The transition from the broad premium multi-blade claw to the support single forearm blade remains visible as the established artwork-role difference; this is not a claim of perfectly identical weapon silhouettes.

The single pale green/silver forearm weapon stays identifiable across premium/HQ/polish. The unarmed white-bandaged hand is visible where the pose exposes it; hands hidden by long hair are not counted as missing. No duplicate weapon, duplicated hand, cropped extremity or major head/torso proportion change was seen in these samples.

findings.evidence: signature Back 0062 versus 0068; original HQ reference row1/col2 and Polish reference row4/col2
findings.observation: The lowered weapon is on screen-right in polish recovery and screen-left in HQ idle. Direct rereading of the two original reference sheets shows the same difference (velvet-polish_3_1 versus velvet-hq_0_1). This visible inherited hand/weapon-side inconsistency remains; it was not introduced by the current candidate or classified as a new automatic facing reversal. The review does not claim perfect left/right anatomical consistency of the original poses.
The figure and exposed limbs remain inside the frame. No obvious detached body fragment, missing full character or second hand-mounted long weapon was found at the displayed capture scale.

limits: Only the listed 37 stills from six 74-frame clips were visually inspected. This is not full real-time playback or a visual review of all 1433 final-b PNGs, all skills, or signature Left/Right continuous motion.

At the fixed 960x540 camera scale the illustrated body occupies roughly 100 image pixels vertically in many views. Major silhouette/weapon duplication and body-size changes are readable, but individual fingers, exact blade count within the one claw, and native line sharpness are not certified.
Native sheet review and prior static optical review remain separate evidence. This sampled pass does not replace the earlier all-pose art review.
Dark isolated captures have no visible floor. This review cannot establish physical foot planting, exact pivot correctness or full root-motion continuity from boot screen coordinates.
Different crouches, lunges, twists, hair and coat spreads legitimately change silhouette bounds. No body-scale conclusion was based on sprite rectangles or total bounding-box height alone.
The inherited Back weapon-side discrepancy and premium-versus-support weapon silhouette difference are explicitly retained observations, not silently approved as perfect consistency.
The candidate-preview result and preserved originals do not establish production replacement or visual approval of a final release build.
